clue.text: Place to relax from Chinese disease

parts.note: the Han are the majority ethnic group of China
gout is a painful joint disease

explanation.surface: A recommendation of somewhere to unwind, or an odd claim that a Chinese illness offers rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal haunt where friends gather to relax is a favourite spot of this kind.

clue.text: Possibly Rumpole's vehicle will turn up in garden

indicators.note: the overturned vehicle is placed in the garden verb

parts.note: to hoe is to work in the garden

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a barrister's car will appear in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumpole of the Bailey is a British TV and fiction barrister whose first name this is; the definition reads 'possibly Rumpole's first name'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the given name of John Mortimer's fictional barrister, one example of the name.

clue.text: Explorer gutted with ancient stewed fruit

indicators.note: stewed means cooked into a mess, so the letters are mixed up
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: An old explorer, disembowelled, with stewed fruit: a grim cooking story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves ER from Explorer; 'stewed' shuffles ER and ANCIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach is a stone fruit.

clue.text: Ancient yellow head mislaid

indicators.note: the head of the word is lost, so its first letter is removed

parts.note: golden is a yellow colour

explanation.surface: An old blond person who has lost their head.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word means belonging to a long-past time, like old or antique.

clue.text: A lot of water a must as man's eating sandwiches

indicators.note: the phrase sandwiches the letters between its outer parts, holding them within

explanation.surface: Insists a person has to drink a great deal while eating sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but is a verb: the phrase encloses the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This stretch of ocean between Australia and New Zealand is a large body of sea.

clue.text: Soiled apparel remains in flight

indicators.note: the remains are placed in the middle of the word for flight

parts.note: on the wing means in flight; a wing is the organ of flight
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Suggests dirty clothes left behind on an aeroplane after a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry waiting to be cleaned is dirty clothing, so soiled apparel is a fair description.

clue.text: I'm enjoying this left turn

parts.note: 'Whee!' is a cry of delight

explanation.surface: A happy driver or dancer delighting in a left turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To swing round in a circle, as troops do, is to pivot or rotate.

clue.text: Carefully protect Peter mixing a drug

parts.note: in criminal slang a peter is a safe

indicators.note: mixing means the letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: Peter is concocting a drug carefully and protectively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a man's name but is criminals' slang for a strongbox; 'mixing' rearranges A DRUG.
explanation.definitionFit: To shield something from harm by precautions is to defend or secure it.

clue.text: Here in 21, I'm thinking, is much colder

parts.note: 21 is the country whose word for here is ici
er is the sound of someone thinking or hesitating

explanation.surface: A speaker hesitates while remarking that it is far chillier somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 21 is a French-speaking country, so 'here' becomes the French word ICI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with more frost is chillier, the comparative of frozen-sounding weather.

clue.text: Starts to go around Debenham's to buy a handy tool

indicators.note: the starts of these words are their initial letters

parts.note: to get something is to buy it

explanation.surface: A shopping trip around Debenham's, a former British department store chain, to purchase a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mechanical device or contraption is useful for particular jobs.

clue.text: Ran club, possibly in Rutherford

indicators.note: the card goes inside the symbol for the unit named in the clue

parts.note: the rutherford is an old unit of radioactivity, symbol Rd
an ace is a card that may be from the club suit

explanation.surface: Reads as someone who managed a club in Rutherford, a town or person's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran' looks like part of the managing story but is the definition, a past-tense verb for sprinting. The rutherford is a unit of radioactivity, a nod to the chemist Ernest Rutherford.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe moving at speed on foot in the past tense, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: 13 on which Tommy wanted to 1A the 5A feeds rig I constructed

definitions.text: 13 on which Tommy wanted to 1A the 5A

indicators.note: constructed means built out of these letters in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wartime reference to a British soldier's song, with a stray instruction about a rig.
explanation.walkthrough: With 13 and the cross-references filled in, the definition reads as the 1939 song 'We're Going to Hang Out the Washing on the Siegfried Line'; Tommy is the British soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The song names Germany's western fortifications, so the definition names the German defensive barrier the soldiers mocked.

clue.text: Armour written about in Malachi

indicators.note: written about suggests the letters are moved around in the writing, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Implies the Old Testament book of Malachi describes armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Interlinked metal rings made a flexible protective garment worn by medieval soldiers.

clue.text: It's prickly buying or selling trousers

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the phrase pockets the letters within it

explanation.surface: Suggests that trousers are uncomfortable whether bought or sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like a noun for clothing but is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: This shrub of heath and moorland is covered in sharp spines, so it is a spiky plant.

clue.text: Pound home point of fishing tackle

parts.note: L, from the Latin libra, abbreviates a pound
being in means being at home
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice to hammer home the tip of an angler's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers cast a cord with hook attached, part of the gear known as tackle.

clue.text: Chopper for one British consumer

parts.note: EG (for example) means for one
GB stands for Great Britain
an eater consumes food

explanation.surface: Suggests a helicopter or axe for a single British customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' is slang for a helicopter, and an eggbeater is also slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a helicopter, whose rotor whirls like a kitchen whisk.

clue.text: Strange bloke, Sam — like a pipe, perhaps

indicators.note: strange tells us the following letters appear in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A description of an odd man called Sam who resembles a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco in a pipe is fit to be puffed, so a pipe holds stuff suitable for inhaling.

clue.text: Exchanging parts when announcing exits is more important

indicators.note: the two parts of the spoken phrase swap places, front half to the back
announcing means saying aloud, so a sound-alike gives the answer

parts.note: exits are ways out

explanation.surface: A comment on announcements at doors in theatres or airports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when announcing' turns WAYS OUT into WEIGHS OUT by sound, and 'Exchanging parts' swaps the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: When one consideration counts for more than another, it carries the greater weight.

clue.text: Directions help with plate that is repaired very quickly, some say

definitions.text: that is repaired very quickly, some say

parts.note: an L-plate shows a learner driver, so plate gives L
two compass directions: east in full and S for south
aid is help

explanation.surface: Instructions for fixing a plate rapidly, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the proverb 'least said, soonest mended'. L-plates mark British learner drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that saying little about a quarrel lets it heal fastest.

clue.text: Gets near corrupt police officer

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tale of someone approaching a crooked policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' seems to describe the officer, but it is the anagram signal working on 'Gets near'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rank in British police forces, above constable and below inspector.

clue.text: Expensive Dutch audio equipment

parts.note: the ear is the body's own hearing apparatus

explanation.surface: A complaint that hi-fi gear from the Netherlands costs a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something costly carries a high price, and that is a common meaning of the word.

clue.text: Insect queen

parts.note: a moth is an insect
ER, Elizabeth Regina, denotes the queen

explanation.surface: Simply names the head of an insect colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen bee or ant is the parent of the whole colony.

clue.text: Tours location of smell left by German artist

indicators.note: the German and artist letters depart from the smell

parts.note: a fragrance is a smell
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Describes where a German painter left an odour on his travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tours' looks like trips but is the city on the Loire.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of Tours lies in this European country, so it is its location.

clue.text: Yellow mineral companion found inside

indicators.note: the companion is placed inside the mineral word

parts.note: ore is a mineral from which metal is extracted
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a yellowish mineral discovered in a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow mineral' reads as one phrase, but only 'Yellow' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The earthy pigment is a brownish-yellow shade, so it names the colour.

clue.text: Sensed one hiding among cattle?

indicators.note: the one is concealed within the cattle word

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle
a means one

explanation.surface: A person who sensed a lone animal concealed in a herd.
explanation.definitionFit: Perceiving a sound by ear is one way of having sensed something.

clue.text: Spooner telling child to cry a river, possibly

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the initial sounds of words, so his saying is given with its openings exchanged

parts.note: to weep is to cry
a daughter is a child

explanation.surface: Pictures a parent telling their child to cry a river of tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner says 'Weep, daughter', swapping W and D to give the answer by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A river may be deep enough to be over your head, an example of such a body.

clue.text: Corrupt police officer oddly ratty

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: A bent policeman who is strangely bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ratty' means irritable in British usage, but here it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest dealings are often called foul or crooked, matching this sense.

clue.text: Agreement to fulfil orders with the Italian firm

parts.note: il is Italian for the
CO abbreviates company, a firm

explanation.surface: Describes a contract to supply goods with an Italian company.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio jargon for 'will comply', said to confirm instructions will be carried out.

clue.text: Gather hoodlum accepts rule for where to let sleeping dogs lie

definitions.text: where to let sleeping dogs lie

parts.note: to gather is to learn by hearing

indicators.note: the hoodlum takes the rule letter inside himself

parts.note: a thug is a violent hoodlum

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction about a thug, a rule and resting dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'let sleeping dogs lie' to mean literally a dog's resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug in front of the fireplace is a favourite warm spot for a pet to doze.

clue.text: Find out Rector Slope's around

indicators.note: the slope wraps itself around the rector's letter

parts.note: to lean is to slope; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: Invites discovering that Mr Slope, the clergyman in Trollope's Barchester novels, is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to come to know it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Soldiers back around Germany? That's amazing!

indicators.note: the back word goes around the letter for Germany

parts.note: the rear is the back
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
'My!' is an exclamation of astonishment

explanation.surface: Someone astonished that troops are returning to Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the army of the Soviet Union, so it is a body of troops.

clue.text: Long, long ship deserted on river

indicators.note: deserted means emptied, so only the outer letters of the ship are kept

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Evokes a lengthy story of an abandoned vessel on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long, long' looks like emphasis, but it defines a metrical foot.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse, this foot consists of two stressed or lengthy syllables in a row.
